newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina's ruling party boosts parliament majority.
newsitem.headline: Burkina's ruling party boosts parliament majority.

text.p: President Blaise Compaore's ruling party has boosted its majority in Burkina Faso's national assembly by winning all four seats at stake in parliamentary election reruns this week, provisional results show.

The results of Wednesday's reruns, announced by the head of the national election commission, give Compaore's Congress for Democracy and Progress (CDP) party 101 of the 111 seats in the assembly elected on May 11.

The Supreme Court scrapped results in the central Kourittenga constituency and in the northern constituency of Oudalan, citing "numerous irregularities which cast doubt on the sincerity of the vote and affected the results".
Compaore's party won all four seat first time round.
Compaore's allies in the Alliance for Democracy and Federation (ADF) of Minister of State for Integration and African Solidarity Herman Yameogo hold two seats.
Joseph Ki-Zerbo's opposition Party for Democracy and Progress (PDP) holds six seats, the African Democratic Rally (RDA) of former prime minister Gerard Kango Ouedraogo, won two.
Compaore's party held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 army coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed. The constitution initially limited him to one seven-year term.
Parliament in January voted to let him stand as many times as he wants. The next presidential election is due in 1998.
